name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about nine points on the partisan index
Jacqui Irwin holds a large fundraising and cash-on-hand advantage over Sam Gallucci
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96 percent
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot adds some uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's nine-point Democratic lean, Irwin's roughly two-to-one fundraising edge and cash advantage, and markets pricing her near 96 percent all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite the open seat. The forecast sits slightly below the fundamentals-implied margin to reflect the absence of an incumbent and any polling.
model.watch: A late outside-spending surge for Gallucci or a strong top-of-ticket Republican environment in California could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Julia Brownley's retirement leaves this Ventura County-area seat open, but the district retains a nine-point Democratic lean on the partisan index. State assemblymember Jacqui Irwin enters the general election with a clear financial edge, having raised about $1.17 million and holding roughly $458,000 on hand, while Republican Sam Gallucci has raised about $538,000 with under $20,000 remaining. Outside groups have also spent modestly to support Irwin, with no reported opposition spending.

Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96 percent, and no expert raters currently list the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing, all of which point to a Democratic hold, with the open-seat dynamic the main source of residual uncertainty.
